hints: Notice the question asks for the statement that is not correct, so three statements are true particle classifications and one is false.
Recall the two groups of fundamental particles: quarks and leptons - check whether electron, neutrino and antineutrino belong to quarks or leptons.
Recall what combinations of quarks form hadrons: three quarks make a baryon such as the neutron, while a quark plus an antiquark makes a meson.
walkthrough: List the particle types in the statements: antineutrino, electron, neutrino, and neutron, and recall the Standard Model division into fundamental quarks and leptons versus composite hadrons.
Leptons including the electron, neutrino and antineutrino are fundamental particles with no internal quark structure, so an antineutrino is fundamental and a neutrino is a lepton.
Hadrons are composite: baryons such as protons and neutrons are made of three quarks, so a neutron composed of three quarks is correct.
A quark plus an antiquark forms a meson, not an electron, so an electron cannot be made up of a quark and an antiquark because the electron is itself fundamental.
Therefore the only false statement is the one about the electron. This is option B.

options.A: This statement is correct - an antineutrino is a lepton and leptons are fundamental particles with no quark structure.
options.B: This statement is not correct - an electron is a fundamental lepton, whereas a quark plus an antiquark makes a meson.
options.C: This statement is correct - neutrinos belong to the lepton family along with electrons.
options.D: This statement is correct - a neutron is a baryon made of three quarks, specifically $udd$.
